data.description: ![Upload](https://s3.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/virtualprotocolcdn/500x1500_5c8f1c6a44.png)
data.tokenUtility:
$BLEP is the utility and settlement token of the BLEEEP verification economy. Its published functions are:

Verification payments and credits: Checking a public record is always free. New verification work (validating a fresh claim, running the gates on a new strategy, machine-metered checks) is paid, and $BLEP settles it alongside USDC as metered credits.

$BLEP discount: Fees and subscriptions are payable in USDC at par, or in $BLEP at an oracle-checked rate for a discount.

Transparency collateral: A creator stakes $BLEP behind a marketplace listing, and the stake is slashed on-chain if forward performance breaches a floor committed to in advance. This makes a false claim economically expensive, not merely reputational.

Buyback-and-burn sink: A share of protocol fees (about 10% of marketplace subscriptions) routes to a $BLEP buyback-and-burn, and the receipt is anchored like any other record.

Machine access (x402 / ACP): Agents pay per-call, metered access to signals and verification through x402 / ACP.

Roadmap \[In sequence]

Current - Docs & early access: Public documentation, the litepaper, and the early-access waitlist are open

Next - Sealed track & public verification: Calls sealed commit-before-outcome, exposed through a public verification console and NO-GO archive

Scheduled - On-chain anchoring: Daily Merkle root anchored to Robinhood Chain; a second resilience chain is planned for later

Scheduled - Standards & reputation: Track record and NO-GOs written to the ERC-8004 reputation registry; a verifiable, pre-committed prediction scoreboard

Scale - Verification economy: Verification API sold per call (x402 / ACP), resolution-risk radar, institutional-grade safety guardrails
data.additionalDetails:
1\. Build in chat.

Describe a strategy to BLEEEPY in plain language: “fade funding when it goes past this level on BTC and ETH, size flat, no leverage, exit after N hours.” It compiles the description into a BleeepSpec, the frozen definition the engine runs. Users can read the compiled spec, edit any field, or write the spec directly. The natural-language step is a convenience, not a black box. The spec is the source of truth, and every line is inspectable before it runs.

2\. Test it before any capital is at risk.

Run the frozen spec through the validation gate and get a GO, NO\_GO, or INSUFFICIENT verdict with the metrics behind it, before any capital is at risk. A NO-GO indicates which specific test the strategy failed, making clear why it would have died, not just that it did. The user revises and resubmits. What cannot be done is move the passing bar: it is fixed and public.

3\. Set the terms.

Choose the markets, the parameters, the risk limits, and the position sizing.

Go from paper to live, safely. Paper forward-testing runs on real prices with no real orders, on the exact decision path live execution uses, so the paper record is comparable to live behavior, while still being clearly labeled as simulated. Promotion to live capital is a human decision, and live is off by default. When it is on, the Safety Vault sits between the strategy and user funds: session keys, spend caps, a destination whitelist, a circuit breaker, a daily-loss auto-pause, and reconciliation against the exchange.

4\. Subscribe to forward-verified strategies. Allocate to any user’s strategy on the strength of a sealed, on-chain track record rather than a +300% screenshot. A subscription is non-custodial: the subscriber receives the strategy’s live signals and deploys them on their own funds, through their own Safety Vault and a human deploy gate, never an automatic mirror. Browse listings in the strategy marketplace.

5\. Keep logic private, prove results.

Every strategy’s decisions seal and anchor before their outcomes, so a user can keep their own logic private while the resulting track record stays provable to anyone.

For over a century, US county governments have auctioned tax lien certificates — a first-position claim on real property that pays statutory interest of 8–25% per year. It's one of the oldest and most defensive yield assets in America, but access has been limited to institutions and auction insiders.

RoodFi changes that. We tokenize tax lien and tax deed markets and bring them fully onchain, built on Robinhood Chain.

**What's live today**

* A working dApp on Robinhood Chain testnet: roodfi.vercel.app
* Onchain lien markets across 6 US counties (Maricopa AZ, Miami-Dade FL, Cook IL, Harris TX, Wayne MI, Pima AZ)
* Real wallet connect, USDC-settled buy/sell, and portfolio tracking — every transaction verifiable on the explorer
* Smart contracts deployed and open for anyone to test with faucet funds

**How it works**

1. Each lien certificate is issued onchain with its statutory rate, redemption window, and parcel reference embedded
2. Investors fund positions in USDC and earn the statutory rate at redemption
3. A 24/7 secondary market lets holders exit before redemption — no more waiting years for liquidity

**Why $ROOD**

$ROOD is the token behind the RoodFi ecosystem: early access to new lien markets, curation of county offerings, and governance as we move from testnet to real-world lien origination.

**Institutions trade with flow, positioning, and context. Retail trades with vibes. MerryMen changes that.**

For decades, the real edge in markets wasn't speed, it was *information asymmetry*. Options flow, macro interpretation, positioning data, analyst networks: intelligence that institutions pay four-to-six figures a year for, and retail never sees. Retail on the other hand, got the scraps e.g., social media takes, price charts, and “confident strangers” on the internet.

Each returns an independent, sourced read. Then the MerryMen **renders the call** — including the part every other signal product hides: *where the scouts disagree*.

Sometimes the call is bullish. Sometimes bearish. And sometimes it's the most valuable call in markets: **NO TRADE — the story is bullish, but the tape hasn't confirmed it.**

That honesty is the product. One AI gives you an answer. **A council gives you judgment.**

### **Why Robinhood Chain — and why now**

Robinhood already changed retail trading once: commission-free investing put markets in the pockets of over 26 million funded accounts and an entire generation of first-time investors. Now it's doing it again — Robinhood Chain puts the stocks themselves on-chain, and with them, something Wall Street never gave retail: **markets that never close.**

Tokenized equities trade 24/7. No opening bell, no waiting for Monday, no watching futures helplessly while news breaks on a Sunday night. Your favourite stocks, tradeable the moment *you* decide — not the moment an exchange in New York decides for you.

But always-on markets create a new problem: **markets never sleep, and you do.** Institutions solve this with overnight desks, algorithms, and around-the-clock analysts. Retail gets the always-on market without the always-on intelligence — which, alone, is just an invitation to trade tired.

That's the gap MerryMen exists to close. When the venue is 24/7, the intelligence has to be too. MerryMen is the always-on council that reads the tape while you live your life — so the millions of retail traders Robinhood is bringing on-chain aren't just trading *more*, they're trading *informed*.

data.description:
Count the apps holding your money right now.

The marketplace sitting on your NFT. The launchpad you aped into. A DEX with an LP position three tabs deep. A bridge still showing "pending" from Tuesday. Each took custody somewhere, and each has a withdraw button you're trusting a stranger to honor. That's the real tax on being onchain. Not gas. Custody.

RobinLaunchpad's whole argument: the number should be one, and the custodian should be nobody.

It's live at robinlaunchpad.com, on Robinhood Chain — an Arbitrum L2, chainId 4663, where native ETH is both the gas and the money you trade with. No wrapped stand-in to buy first. Desktop and mobile wallets, a 3D "onchain void," ⌘K to jump anywhere. The UI's the fun part, not the thesis. The thesis is one load-bearing phrase: approval, not custody. You sign; the platform never holds your funds.

The NFT marketplace is where that gets tested. List at a fixed price and the NFT never leaves your wallet — the buyer pulls it the second they pay, and that's the only power the contract has. Offers and bids are the exception, because a bid nobody can enforce is just a tweet, so those get escrowed. Auctions run English with anti-snipe: bid in the final seconds and the clock adds ten minutes, so you win by bidding more, not by refreshing faster. Royalties are EIP-2981 up to 10%, auto-split at settlement. Floor sweep clears the bottom shelf in one tx.

Inscriptions use the chain as storage. You write data straight into a transaction as calldata — a data: URI that lives there forever — and it comes back stamped with a sequential ordinal number. Text, images, JSON. Sell a 1/1 through an escrow market that holds it only while it's listed; delist and it's home the same block. No server to go dark on you. There isn't one.

rh-20 stacks a fungible standard on that, BRC-20 in spirit, and the rule that matters is fair launch by construction: no presale, no team bag. Deploy a ticker, mints go first-come-first-served, and you can't sell until it's fully minted out — the deployer crosses the line with everyone else. NFT Drops aim the same discipline at creators: an ERC-721 with a paid public mint in one tx, you set price, supply, per-wallet cap and royalty, you own the contract, proceeds land instantly, overpay refunds itself, no trading until it's 100% minted.

The memecoin launchpad is the pump.fun shape. A token trades the instant it exists with zero seed liquidity, because price runs off a constant-product bonding curve, not a pool someone had to fund. Every buy walks it up. Dev-buy in the launch tx and snipers eat your dust. Creator takes 1% of every trade. At 80% bought it graduates: leftover tokens plus all raised ETH lock into a pool for good — keeps trading, nobody can pull it. There's a shareable PnL card whose art shifts by tier. Mooning, in profit, rekt. Same button for bragging and coping.

Liquidity & Pools is where non-custodial turns into math. A live, auto-detected map of every V2 and V3 pair. Add or remove from the UI, signing each move. V2 fees auto-compound; V3 concentrates a range and shows the exact claimable fees plus whether you're in range or just cosplaying an LP. Swap fees go 100% to LPs, no skim. LP PnL is the honest kind, rebuilt from onchain history with impermanent loss counted, in ETH — and it all rolls into one portfolio, memecoins and NFTs and inscriptions and LP, with allocation and all-time PnL.

The Bridge does a bridge's one job: LI.FI routing through audited bridges from Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, BSC and more into RH Chain. RobinLaunchpad hosts the interface. That's it.

Trading Agents are in beta, and the honest version is short: bring your own AI key, agents pitch trades in character — Degen, Sniper, LP Farmer, ten providers — and they recommend, full stop. Your wallet signs, the key never leaves your browser. Worst case, one talks you into a trade you'd have found by 3am anyway.

Notice what none of it does. The marketplace won't hold your NFT. The launchpads won't sit on the mint. The bridge won't hold your bridge. The agents won't hold your keys. The graduated pool is locked so tight the founders can't reach in. No withdraw button anywhere, because there's nothing to withdraw from. The money was never anywhere but your own wallet.

Go poke at it: robinlaunchpad.com. And @robinlaunchpad if you feel like yelling at us.
